sentences.text: A review by Alan Milburn (left) could create political headaches for Andy Burnham Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He saw how last year's welfare rebellion marked the beginning of the end for his predecessor in Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Sir Keir Starmer's authority was shredded when 120 - more than a quarter - of his own MPs threatened to derail his reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: To defuse this, Sir Keir was compelled to guarantee that existing claimants of personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales, wouldn't lose out.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Even then, 49 of the 120 potential Labour rebels still voted against their own government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Next week, a review from former New Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn has the capacity to create another internal row in Labour's ranks.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn has spent a year grappling with how to reduce the nearly one million young people who are not in employment, education or training (Neets).
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: In an interview with the Times, he has now confirmed he is set to recommend cutting benefits for some 16-24 year olds who currently receive Pip, or the enhanced health-related payment of Universal Credit.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Taking benefit cuts to the Parliamentary Labour Party would usually have a similar effect to adding phosphorous to water.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But from my soundings, the deep waters of the Labour ranks are calmer than might be expected.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Importantly, two of the most effective organisers of last year's welfare rebellion are batting for the current prime minister, rather than against the previous one.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Louise Haigh is now the most powerful cabinet minister after Andy Burnham himself, while Anneliese Midgeley is his chief whip.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And the MP who fronted that rebellion - Meg Hillier - has said she wants to give Milburn's proposals a "fair wind".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There are also clear differences to the previous approach to welfare reform.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: First, it is not being presented as primarily a cost-cutting exercise with pre-determined savings.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Instead, there will be upfront investment to provide more support to unemployed young people, and a timeframe for net savings likely to be set at around a decade – gradualism, not a short, sharp shock.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Second, last year's initial reforms would have affected people in all age groups, whilst benefit cuts this time would be limited to the under 25s, who make up around 11% of Pip claimants.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say One in eight young people still out of work or education ahead of major review I've spoken to government ministers who had expressed concerns – at least privately – about the changes devised previously by Rachel Reeves and Liz Kendall.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: This time, they are on board.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One of them told me that so long as there was enough support for young people, with guaranteed jobs and training, MPs would be "fine" with some benefit cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But they added that it was vital that those who really couldn't work wouldn't be worse off.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn will suggest there could even be enhanced payments for people in this category, while some young people with disabilities who lose out on Pip could nonetheless be given an additional "allowance" to help with living costs.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Another minister who opposed the previous reforms praised the process this time.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There had been a high level of engagement not just from Milburn, but Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden, who has been taking MPs through the principles behind the reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One minister was a little more cautious, suggesting support for a reduction in benefits would depend on what the entire "package" of reforms looked like.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn's recommendations are likely to be wide-ranging – from pre-school policies to how the NHS deals with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some of the eventual 49 rebels from last year are in a similar place.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: York MP Rachael Maskell told me it was essential that she saw the detail of the proposals rather than the "drip, drip" of press reports which would "cause young people stress and distress".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She felt withdrawing Pip from young people was "like a sledgehammer to crack a nut" and was concerned that some disabled people required it to remain in work.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She also suggested that the government "shouldn't just point the finger at young people," and should look closely at how employers could take more youngsters on.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Stroud MP Simon Opher also voted against the government on welfare last year.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He told me there was a "crisis" with so many Neets, and Milburn had come up with a "credible solution".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But he believes cutting benefits should be a "last resort" and is worried about restricting access to the health element of Universal Credit, as a quarter of young claimants aren't Neet.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He concludes that the "devil will be in the detail".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So much of politics - like comedy – depends on timing.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: For some sceptics, including serving ministers, the Milburn proposals will be more warmly welcomed if support for young people is in place before entitlements are withdrawn.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But for some Labour MPs, cutting payments to existing claimants crosses a line.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Clapham and Brixton Hill MP Bell Ribiero-Addy has she wasn't sure she could back cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Referring to Pip, she didn't believe that "you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And another MP on the left of the party, Brian Leishman, told the BBC he couldn't back benefits cuts as "we are in the middle of a cost of living crisis".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So a welfare rebellion seems guaranteed if Burnham accepts Milburn's recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But it seems unlikely to be of the same scale, or have a similar level of political jeopardy to the one which shook the Starmer government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some job applicants in England and Wales would no longer need to declare criminal convictions they received as children under government proposals designed to improve the employment prospects of rehabilitated young people.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: The changes would mean criminal records for people detained when they were under 18 years old would no longer show up for life during checks carried out by employers.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: The Ministry of Justice has also launched a consultation on relaxing disclosure requirements for some specific drug-related and violent crimes committed by children.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Young people who have not re-offended as adults struggle to find work because of their past behaviour, the government says.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Many employers require applicants to undergo a background check, which in their most basic form require people to self-declare if they have a criminal record.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: For more sensitive roles, such as working with children or joining the police, an employer can carry out a standard or enhanced check, which allows them to request information from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: How long a criminal record must be volunteered for or will show up in those checks differs depending on the severity of the offence, the punishment received and how long ago the crime was committed - sometimes referred to as whether a conviction is 'spent'.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: For example, a young person who was convicted and fined for an offence when they were under-18 will have that information show up in checks for five-and-a-half years.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: If they were given a custodial sentence, that will be disclosed for the rest of their lives.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: The government wants to reduce the number of young people those disclosure rules apply to if an applicant has not continued to offend as an adult.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Five offences would be removed from a list of crimes which will show up in background for checks for life if committed by an adult.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: They are: affray, violent disorder, supplying a controlled drug to a child, robbery and assaults occasioning actual bodily harm.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Between March 2022 and March 2026, around 8,500 under-18s were convicted of those offences, according to Ministry of Justice data.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: The government says that type of crime is often a result of peer pressure, exploitation and "adolescent impulsivity" by individuals who are still developing, as opposed to a broader propensity for crime and violence.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Under the new rules, they would cease to show up in checks after five-and-a-half years.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: Lifelong disclosure would also be removed for offences which led to a detention period of less than two years, the maximum which can be handed out by a youth court, and replaced by a new 11-year disclosure period.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: In cases where a child was given a sentence longer than two years - which can only happen if the severity of the crime meant they were dealt with by an adult crown court - the rules would stay the same.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: The most serious offences - including severe violence, terrorism-related crimes and sexual offences - would be exempted from the reforms.
sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: "They take responsibility, turn their lives around and want to make something of themselves.

sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: The court heard that a catalogue of physical and verbal abuse of Farah by Gizzi was unearthed after she made a suspected suicide attempt that left her with severe brain damage.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: In his sentencing remarks, Judge Mills said Farah and her family and friends had faced an "appalling tragedy" and said the case of coercive control was one of the worst the court had seen, telling Gizzi he had subjected her to "appalling" behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Judge Mills said Gizzi had used "dreadful misogynistic language" towards Farah which was "part of the process of humiliation" and "destroying" her self worth.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Farah's mother, wearing a T-shirt saying Justice for Natasha, read a lengthy victim impact statement, saying she wanted to detail the "sheer devastating" impact Gizzi's behaviour had had and the "pain, grief, anger, torture" he had inflicted.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: She described her daughter as "the most beautiful, funniest, kindest soul in the world" and told Gizzi, who was appearing by video link, that he was a "smiling devil monster".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Judge Mills said Natasha was often seen to have bruises, and was once assaulted by Gizzi with a dumbbell.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: "You would accuse her of sleeping with other men… assaulted her frequently… sometimes in front of other people… you assaulted her in front of her child," he said.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: The judge also said Gizzi had assaulted her on Valentine's Day and Mother's Day.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: "She would plead with you to desist," he added.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: John Gizzi was jailed for four years and 11 months He added that a domestic abuse protection order that had been sought did not go ahead because Natasha had asked the magistrates not to proceed, and she "had a note which appeared to tell her what to say".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: He said that when Farah's sister Samantha had challenged Gizzi, his response had been violent.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: "You gripped her neck with your hands, she fell to floor... there were marks on her neck." Earlier the court heard further details of what had happened prior to 7 April when Farah was found having attempted suicide at her flat in Rhos on Sea by Gizzi, who phoned the emergency services.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Elen Owen, prosecuting, the told the court it was not the Crown's case that Gizzi was responsible, but the discovery of Farah led to an investigation that unearthed a catalogue of physical and verbal abuse of her by Gizzi.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Owen outlined a long list of attacks and abuse inflicted by Gizzi on Farah between March 2025 and April 2026.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: It included an attack on her at a gym the pair used when she arrived to ask for some keys, which Gizzi threw at her and hit her in the face.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Another man stepped in to protect her.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Farah told a friend of a second physical assault at the same gym.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: He repeatedly followed her, attacked her in her car and left countless messages using abusive language.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Natasha's mother (fifth from the left) was among her supporters campaigning outside court on Thursday In September 2025, Farah was found after another apparent suicide attempt, and a call to the emergency services recorded Gizzi physically and verbally abusing Farah's mother, Denise.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: The police were informed but Denise later withdrew the complaint.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Some of his abuse was caught on public CCTV cameras, and following one such incident in January 2025, Gizzi was arrested.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Police tried to get a domestic protection order but Farah decided not to co-operate and magistrates declined to make the order.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Her sister Samantha witnessed repeated abuse and was herself attacked by Gizzi at a pub in Colwyn Bay - that led to a charge of strangulation, one of three Gizzi pleaded guilty to at a hearing last month.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: The former drug gang boss also pleaded guilty to refusing to give police the pin so they could access his phone.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Messages found on it included a stream of abuse and messages from Farah saying he had made her feel "worthless" and had "broken" and "crushed" her.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Referring to the assaults on Boxing Day and Valentine's Day, Farah told Gizzi: "I don't have one good memory with you".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: He responded with an abusive message.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: In a message where she referred to him kicking her leg, he replied: "I couldn't reach your face".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Judge Mills told the court that he must recognise the events of 7 April that had left Farah "in an unresponsive state with serious brain damage"  but said there was no offence in the indictment making Gizzi directly responsible.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: He added that he had "no doubt" that if "circumstances were to change or further evidence came to light" that would be investigated by North Wales Police but it was "not a matter for today".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: The judge told Gizzi he was "never going to be forgiven for what people believe you did to her" and said that would "follow" him through his life.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: He added, to applause from the public gallery, that people who had been afraid of him "were no longer".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Outside court, friends and family of Farah gathered to express their anger at Gizzi's sentence, with her mother Denise saying she would continue to campaign in her daughter's name for sentences around coercive and controlling behaviour to be longer.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: She described violence against women and girls as an "epidemic".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.text: Gizzi also received a concurrent four-month sentence for failing to supply the pin number for his mobile device to the police after his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner

sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: The shooting began on Thursday morning local time inside a gym in an apartment building in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, which is about a mile (1.6km) north of the White House.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Police said the male suspect was "contained" after barricading himself in one of the apartments.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: They later confirmed he had died.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Of those injured, one is in a critical condition and the others have non-life-threatening injuries.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: While the suspect was barricaded, "he did fire through the door at officers at least on two occasions", Jefferey Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, said at a news conference.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Negotiators had been on the phone with the suspect when they heard a gunshot and he stopped communicating with them, according to Carroll.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Officers forced their way into the apartment and saw the suspect had what appeared to be a "self-inflicted gunshot wound", he said.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Carroll added that police "believe there was a fire that was set", which has been contained.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Authorities are still working to understand the exact timeline, suspect's motivation, and other details of the incident.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: "We believe there was some sort of a conflict with the apartment building, but we don't have much more than that," Carroll said.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Washington DC Mayor Muriel Bowser called it a "senseless act of gun violence" and said the White House had been briefed.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: A BBC producer who lives in the building where the shooting happened, Jonathan Csapo, said a fire alarm went off.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Then, as he came out of a fire escape, he heard gunshots very close by.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: "I could see the smoke, I could see the flash.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: We just all started running.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: That was our first instinct," he said.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: "We immediately ran and took cover behind a barricade, a little brick structure just near the building." Csapo said he was then taken back inside, to a safe room, by a building manager.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: "And then everybody started screaming," he said.
sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.article_title: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured as suspect dies after standoff

sentences.text: Alan Milburn will publish his review next week Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: As reported in the Times, , external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet".
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: It is available to those both in and out of work.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: In his interim report, , external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets , data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Dame Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Student Tom said he relies on the money he gets from Pip to support him through his time at university He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear".
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details, families were "deeply anxious".
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: Responding on Thursday, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the government should not be spending "lots of time" on employment schemes, which she said would ultimately fail.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month.
sentences.article_title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say

sentences.text: A snail-eating horned frog discovered in India has been named Jingophrys tanogogo Scientists have discovered five new species of tiny horned frogs in India's eastern Himalayas, more than doubling the number of known species in the group.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: A team of scientists from University of Delhi and Harvard University made the discoveries after five years of fieldwork, identifying the frogs as members of the Jingophrys group.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: Among them is Jingophrys tanogogo - or the snail-eating horned frog - the first frog known in India to feed on snails and the first member of its family recorded with such a diet.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: The research suggest the Himalayas have played a much larger role in frog evolution than previously thought and highlight the region as an overlooked hotspot for biodiversity.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: Despite drawing interest from scientists and researchers, many parts here have not been fully explored.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: The state of Arunachal Pradesh particularly has emerged as one of its least-studied regions.
sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: Dr Sonali Garg, who led the study at Harvard University's Museum of Comparative Zoology, said the research highlights how significant evolutionary changes can go unnoticed in little-studied species.

sentences.text: The study - called two-fold hidden diversity of diminutive horned frogs (Megophryinae: Jingophrys) - was conducted by Garg along with her colleague James Hanken and Delhi University's SD Biju, Tage Tajo and Radhakrishna Upadhyaya K.

sentences.article_title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas

sentences.text: Researchers say they will have to carry out more studies to better understand the biology of the new species, including Jingophrys siangensis ( Siang horned frog) "Some of the new species are extremely secretive and found in remote forests only during a short breeding season," says Biju.

sentences.text: DNA analysis showed the horned frogs rapidly diversified into multiple species in the eastern Himalayas as the mountain range rose and the Asian monsoon took shape over millions of years, helping drive the evolution of the region's plants and wildlife.

sentences.text: The researchers said in a statement that local tribes gave them essential field support and knowledge that helped make the discoveries possible.

sentences.text: Poundland has avoided immediate collapse after a deadline was extended to find a rescue deal.

sentences.text: Computer programming and consultancy services in particular contributed to overall growth (generic photo) ﻿The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures , external show.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the Office for National Statistics, said it was "possible growth could have been even stronger" if there hadn't been a war in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: But he says households may still not feel better off, and that prices might soon start to rise more quickly than wages.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: "Despite a year where events around the world have pushed up costs here at home, our economy is growing, bringing hope for the future," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey told the BBC the figures showed a "remarkable resilience" in the face of global conflicts, and hopes they "bring back confidence in Britain".
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Asked about how government decisions could be the reason for growth when AI investment has been a main driver, Healey said ministers can always "help or hinder" business confidence and investments.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Although investors have recently been concerned about slower artificial intelligence development in the US and the long term viability of AI firms' business models, businesses have continued to invest in the technologies.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Sarah Coles, from investment platform AJ Bell, said that since the start of the year, "it's the less visible back-office work that has delivered, with administrative and supportive services seeing strong growth" noting that these are the areas benefitting from the increasing use of AI.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: A sharp rise in energy bills is forecast for January, which is likely to hit consumer spending and confidence, he said.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: High energy costs have been stoked by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: US and Israeli attacks led to Iran blocking the Strait of Hormuz - a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Russia and Ukraine have been attacking each other's oil refineries, leading to a squeeze on global refining capacity, hitting diesel and petrol prices.

sentences.text: Old landfill and industrial sites have been major sources of the chemicals in rivers like the Mersey Levels of the two most toxic "forever" chemicals in England's rivers have dropped by nearly a third over the last decade, according to new figures from the Environment Agency (EA).
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The decline in the chemicals, PFOS and PFOA, has been put down to stricter restrictions on their use in products after increasing evidence emerged of their damaging impact on human health and the environment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One expert studying the impact of the chemicals said it was "brilliant" to see how far the UK has come on this issue.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Thousands of other forever chemicals, known officially as PFAS, remain in use but the regulator said its report showed the need for them all to be better monitored and regulated.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: PFAS were first developed in the 1930s in the US and became popular with companies making products like frying pans and firefighting foam because of their useful, oil-resistant, water-resistant and electrical properties.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: They are called forever chemicals because their natural resistance means they take a very long time to break down naturally.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The earliest types of these chemicals were called PFOS and PFOA.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: But two decades ago researchers started to find that they were linked to tissue damage in animals and increased rates of certain serious health conditions such as testicular cancer. , external As a result, PFOS was all but banned in the UK in 2010 and PFOA in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The latest data from the regulator, published on Thursday, shows that the concentrations in English rivers of PFOS and PFOA over the last 10 years have now fallen by 30% and 29% respectively.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Levels in freshwater fish have fallen 49%.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "It's brilliant to see how far we have come in the last 10 years," said Dr David Megson, reader in environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: There are thought to be around 15,000 other PFAS, although only around 200 are frequently used.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA said that despite increasing research into these compounds, "uncertainty remains regarding the toxicity of many PFAS".
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: It said its findings "reinforces the need" for regulating all PFAS rather than one by one.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The chemicals industry has long opposed such an approach, arguing that there is currently no, or limited, evidence to suggest that other PFAS are toxic and that some have vital uses such as in life-saving medical equipment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The regulator is now regularly testing for 60 other PFAS to build a picture of contamination across the country, and earlier this month the government announced that it would begin monitoring levels in people's bodies.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA report acknowledged that while concentration levels had fallen, because the chemicals take so long to break down, the overall amount still in the environment is likely to have remained unchanged - they have simply been diluted and been washed into the sea.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "There is a lot to do, and this report provides an essential foundation to support investigations to make the polluters pay for any damage they have caused," said Megson.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One of the few ways to permanently destroy PFAS is by high-temperature incineration - there are currently just two such suitable sites in the country.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Cancer charities and doctors say sunbeds are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers A watchdog has launched a crackdown on misleading sunbed adverts, warning tanning firms they must not claim their beds are safe or can treat medical conditions.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: The Committee for Advertising Practice (CAP) said it was issuing a UK-wide enforcement notice to "send a clear message to the industry that advertisers must not downplay the risks associated with sunbed use".

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the BBC identified hundreds of social media videos claiming the beds could boost energy and treat skin conditions or mental health problems.

sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Sunbeds carry serious health risks, including an increased risk of skin cancer," said the CAP's compliance executive James Burnett.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Ads shouldn't downplay those risks or present sunbed use as a way to improve health." Cancer charities and doctors are clear about the risks of using sunbeds - and say the machines are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers.

sentences.text: Using a bed before the age of 35 increases the risk of melanoma by 59% later in life, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Young people are by far the biggest sunbed users in the UK - about one in seven 18-to-24-year-olds say they used one in the past year, double the average for all age groups, according to a 2025 YouGov survey.

sentences.text: "We want young people to be properly informed about the risk of sunbed use and we recommend using trusted, regulated sources to find out information such as the NHS , external or cancer charities , external ," she added.

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It is a true engineering marvel.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Engine-makers continually vie for access to the technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Rolls-Royce, GE and France's Safran are among the few firms that have perfected the process.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Neither company responded to BBC News' requests for comment but the move has been described as an effort to ensure supply of these critical components.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Separately, in March, Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham blade casting facility.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Turbine blade specialists continue to work on improving the capabilities of this little-known technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: To grow one of these blades, asserts Fifoot, is to "fight the laws of the universe".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: This is because each molten blade would naturally cool into a solid object consisting of many small grains of metal alloy, all jumbled together.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But you don't want a crumbly sugar cube, you want a perfect diamond.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Getting a single crystal to grow into the shape of the blade instead isn't just a matter of cooling the molten version down slowly, the process also uses a bizarre trick called a pigtail.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: "This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables – that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Last week, head of the association Mike Hawes said transitioning to electric vehicles had come at a "heavy cost" with billions spent on discounts to drive demand in electric vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: He said the government's targets could not be achieved "without putting at risk any future investment".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The government's policy to phase out petrol and diesel vehicle sales has undergone multiple changes since it was first introduced by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: His successor Rishi Sunak pushed back the timeline to 2035, and the Burnham government set up a review of the EV sales targets in August.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Sunak introduced phased targets for EV sales in the UK, known as the Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV) mandate.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The target was 28% for 2025, 33% for 2026, and so on until it reaches 80% by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Pressure in the European Union saw the bloc scrap a similar plan to ban new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035, particularly from countries with large auto industries such as Germany.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The Conservative Party has also vowed to abandon the petrol car ban if it wins the next election, with leader Kemi Badenoch calling it a "well-meaning, but ultimately destructive piece of legislation".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the government was "building up a shocking record of backsliding and bad decisions on climate issues".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Kieran Kyle said Kemi Badenoch would get "a bullet in her head" if she went to Belfast, the court heard A man has been jailed for sending the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch emails threatening to shoot her dead.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Ex-teacher Kieran Kyle sent three emails on 2 May to the Tory party leader in which he made racist references and claimed to have been in the IRA, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The 43-year-old, from Gillingham in Kent, pleaded guilty on 22 September at Westminster Magistrates' Court to two counts of sending communications of an indecent or offensive nature.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Kyle was sentenced to 20 weeks in prison at the same court on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: In a victim impact statement read to the court, Badenoch and her husband Hamish said the "malicious communications and targeted harassment" not only had an effect on them, but also undermined "a healthy democracy".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: In two of the emails, Kyle had made racist references and written: "I'm ex-IRA, so Bloody Sunday references from you are going to give you trouble," the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The messages were sent on the day Badenoch apologised for footage from Bloody Sunday being mistakenly used in a social media clip to criticise a parliamentary Bill on legacy issues in Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The Tory leader had said she did not sign off the video and that it was sent out by "very young people".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The video criticising the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, posted to her social media channels on 28 April, showed Badenoch saying the Labour legislation would "drag" Troubles veterans back to court.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Thirteen unarmed civilians were shot dead when members of the Army's Parachute Regiment opened fire on civil rights demonstrators in the Bogside area of Londonderry on 30 January 1972, a date that became known as Bloody Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The court heard Kyle had also sent an email to Badenoch's husband Hamish on 29 April, which used a racist term and said she had a "big mouth" and he should "put a leash on her".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The Tory leader was said to have been left upset and distressed by the messages Prosecutor Ben Holt said the North West Essex MP and her husband were left "distressed" and "upset", particularly by the "racist language and threats of violence used towards them".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: He added Cheryl Bacon, head of Badenoch's parliamentary office, said the emails were "disgusting" and "distressing" to read.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Baiju Thittala, defending, told the court Kyle "did not know" who Badenoch was at the time of the offences, adding "he only realised later, once he had sent the emails".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Asked by the judge how Kyle, a former secondary school teacher, could not know who Badenoch was, Thittala said: "He just 'Googled' it and it came up as the opposition leader." The judge said: "The first emails were sent to Mr Badenoch, so I don't think he did not appreciate who Mrs Badenoch was.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: "When individuals choose to intimidate, threaten, or aggressively target elected representatives or public figures, the harm extends far beyond any single person.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: It undermines a healthy democracy." The continued: "Public service relies on people being willing to step forward, often at significant personal cost, to represent their communities and contribute to public life.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: "Increasingly, however, those who do so face hostility, harassment, and attempts to silence or intimidate them." The judge also handed Kyle a restraining order, meaning he cannot contact Badenoch, her husband or her parliamentary office for five years.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats
