sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Chris Cash says counter-terror officers entered his bedroom and arrested him A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The two men consistently maintained their innocence.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said he denied any wrongdoing and that he had been "unfairly subjected to a trial by media".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He said he had provided reports to a Chinese company, which he believed had clients seeking to develop trading links with the UK, and those reports contained no classified information and relied on public sources.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash returned to the UK in 2019, saying in his resignation message for his job in China that he felt "guilty sitting back and participating in a system that I am uncomfortable with".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He later became the director of a small policy group run by China-sceptic Conservative MPs in Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Berry stayed in China writing reports for a large consultancy which, like many Chinese companies, has links to the government.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: England and Wales' top prosecutor said the case had collapsed last autumn because government officials could not say China had been classed as an "enemy" at the time.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: This prompted accusations of UK political interference to placate the Chinese government.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: China has previously called the allegations of spying "pure fabrication and malicious slander".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The most striking section of the messages handed to the BBC concerns Berry's account of his meeting in summer 2022 with a senior Chinese official who wanted to have "a more detailed co-operation".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In voice notes Berry describes how, beforehand, work colleagues had told him the official's interest had been piqued by reports Berry had written, which included details of the UK's foreign policy approach to China.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The experience "felt like a psychological game of chess" and "like a test", Berry says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He kept his hands under the table as tea was served: "I didn't want it to be obvious if I was nervous.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: I tested to see if my hands were shaking first, then drank the tea." Berry describes the senior Chinese official asking via an interpreter "about the situation in the UK at the moment, about the Tory leadership thing".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: At that time, Boris Johnson had just resigned as the UK's prime minister, and a Conservative leadership battle was taking place, which Liz Truss would go on to win.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry says he jokingly tried to ask his host which candidate China wanted, but the interpreter did not translate his question.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "And then the main guy just shakes my hand like it's time to go," Berry tells Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: After receiving the voice notes, Cash replies via text the next day: "You, my friend, have just been elite captured" before adding: "You're in spy territory now".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In many media reports these particular messages, previously released in a government witness statement, have been presented as a smoking gun - evidence that Cash knew his friend was passing on information to the Chinese state.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But Cash insists it was a "tongue-in-cheek joke" because he knew his friend to be "a staunch critic of the Chinese Communist Party".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The next morning, he made a joke about Berry spying for the UK and getting in trouble with the Chinese authorities, he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash texted: "Keep him sweet… We may have a use for you yet".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I didn't believe he was knowingly spying on the UK through me," says Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I trusted my friend… I wish I had seen the danger earlier, spotted it and cut off all contact." So who was the mystery official Berry had met?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I found out who this guy is," Berry text-messaged Cash a few hours later.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Bigger deal than I thought." Berry posted a link to the Wikipedia page of Cai Qi, who at the time was one of China's most influential politicians and is now, in effect, President Xi Jinping's chief of staff.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry identified Cai Qi (left) as the man he had met - a trusted aide of Chinese President Xi Jinping Whether Berry correctly identified his host remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He has since disputed the suggestion that he met someone as senior as Cai Qi.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: What is beyond dispute is that he believed he may have met someone highly placed within the Chinese political system.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: For Chris Cash, this unusual encounter did not prompt alarm bells.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Asked why not, Cash tells the BBC: "Because I didn't think anything of the meeting, really." We ask Cash why his friend might have been asked to such a meeting.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Strange things happen in China... you know we would often brush shoulders with sort of quite senior members of the Chinese communist party," he tells us.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Challenged about whether he had read the Wikipedia link at the time, Cash says he had "skimmed it", adding that it described him as a judge and a provincial-level official.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I just thought it was a weird meeting with a guy who'd taken an interest," he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Six months later, Berry said in text messages that "off the record" he had it "on pretty good authority" that China was considering dropping sanctions against Tom Tugendhat, one of the Conservative MPs in the China Research Group, where Cash worked.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry wrote that this would happen as long as the West "continued to show signals that they are willing to work together".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The Chinese believed it would be "extremely embarrassing" if Tugendhat became prime minister or foreign secretary while under Chinese sanctions, Berry said.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: At the time of the meeting in summer 2022, China-sceptic Tugendhat was seen as a possible contender to succeed Boris Johnson, or become UK foreign secretary.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He was actually appointed as security minister by Liz Truss, and Beijing lifted sanctions on him in January 2026.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Was Cash concerned that Berry appeared to be passing information to him about Chinese foreign policy?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he assumed Berry had heard this "through the grapevine at his company" which was doing business with the UK.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He says he never doubted his friend's trustworthiness, to the extent he even named Berry as a reference on his application for a security pass for the Palace of Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The pass was granted and, a fortnight before their arrests in early 2023, Cash invited Berry to Parliament for lunch.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: It was to be their final face-to-face conversation.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash was in bed at quarter to six on a March morning when he was woken by car doors being shut, he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Within seconds, four UK counter-terrorism officers had barged into his bedroom at his parents' home in Edinburgh.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "They told me to sit up and not touch anything and then said I was under arrest for breaching the Official Secrets Act," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I was in complete shock… quivering...
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: My mum was hysterical." Cash says the officers dressed him in dirty clothes he had worn that weekend, handcuffed him and marched him down to an unmarked police car.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He was later driven to London.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Chris Berry was also arrested the same day.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: It remains unclear how, when and why British security services became interested in the exchanges between the two friends.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But they are likely to have found out far more about their relationship when Berry was stopped and questioned by counter-terror officers at Heathrow Airport.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: His laptop and phone were taken - this may have enabled his Signal chats to be downloaded.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry later messaged Cash about it.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The allegations were based on 6,273 messages between the pair - the same ones Cash has now shared with the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash's solicitor has told the BBC they are genuine.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: They cover a period when Cash had joined the China Research Group (CRG), founded by Tugendhat and fellow Tory MP Alicia Kearns, and when Berry was working for a Chinese company called Strong, where part of his work involved writing political and economic reports for clients.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: According to court documents, Berry was said to have compiled 34 reports for a man linked to the Chinese state spy agency, relaying information passed on to him by Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Strong did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The CRG's office was across the Thames from Westminster, but Cash regularly had meetings in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash did not have government security clearance and there is no evidence he had access to classified documents.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Despite being thousands of miles apart, the two friends remained in close contact, often messaging daily.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages reviewed by the BBC show them discussing topics including sanctions on China, the tech company Huawei, human rights, Hong Kong, Taiwan and British foreign policy.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he used the Signal app for almost all his contacts with people in China - "more for their protection" - as he says discussing the government "could land someone… in trouble".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He and Berry did not use the app's "disappearing messages" function.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Much of the information they discussed was publicly available, says Cash - who has given the BBC a detailed spreadsheet with links and references in an attempt to prove it.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But sometimes he did share with Berry his impressions from meetings and private discussions in Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: On 12 occasions in the messages, he labelled information "off the record" or "very off the record" before passing it on.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says this was "just me excitedly sharing things that I was doing with him at work".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: One message recounted views allegedly expressed in private by Britain's then-ambassador to China, Dame Caroline Wilson, during a discussion with the CRG about its work on China's influence on UK universities.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash also messaged Berry sharing unverified rumours about the sex lives of two UK cabinet ministers.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: There is no evidence Berry passed this to his Chinese colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he regarded such exchanges as routine political discussion.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "We weren't working with classified information," he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash was told by his solicitor the police investigation would blow over after six months and he would soon be able to return to normal life.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But in September 2023 - six months after the arrests - the case became public when the Sunday Times broke the story of an unnamed "spy" who had been arrested in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash recalls travelling on a train while, around him, fellow passengers read the  newspaper's front page story: "Commons 'Chinese spy' arrested".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He says: "I wanted the world to eat me up." Within 24 hours he was named and pictured in the press, and both men were later charged with espionage.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In September the following year, just weeks before their trial was due to begin, Cash received an unexpected call from his solicitor.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Are you sitting down?" he asked Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "They've dropped all the charges." His lawyers requested a court hearing for the prosecution to formally acknowledge that they would offer no evidence, but at the Old Bailey the newly-innocent Cash struggled to find anyone interested in his story.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash's life has changed almost beyond recognition, he says, but he is positive about the future At every previous court appearance he had been mobbed, but the press had not been informed about this hearing.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Eventually his team found a lone BBC journalist.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I said my piece outside the Old Bailey.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: And that was a real high point.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Growing up in a council flat in the 1980s and 1990s, my mum would often point out homes that tenants had bought from the council.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: You could usually tell just from looking.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: New windows had appeared.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Sometimes there was a porch or pillars outside the front door.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Those houses were bought under the Right to Buy scheme - arguably the most consequential housing policy of my lifetime.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: It was introduced in 1980, three years before I was born, when Margaret Thatcher's government gave council tenants in England the legal right to purchase their homes at a discounted price.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Supporters welcomed the chance for working-class families to own their own home and build wealth.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Critics argue it hollowed out the country's stock of social housing and contributed to today's housing crisis.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Some of my neighbours "made a killing" from the policy, in the words of my mum.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: One bought an almost identical flat to ours in 1989 for £21,200, after receiving a discount of £18,800.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Eight years later it sold for £54,500.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: The Right to Buy scheme has seen various changes since its introduction in the 1980s, and Labour has weakened it significantly since coming to power in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Then, in September, the prime minister told Labour's conference: "We will reform Right to Buy.

sentences.text: Not taking the right away from anyone in an existing home, but removing it from new homes." This would help to keep council houses in public ownership "for generations to come", Burnham told delegates.

sentences.text: He has previously compared trying to solve the housing crisis while continuing to sell social homes to "trying to fill a bath with the plug out".
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: More than 40 years after its introduction, Right to Buy remains a debate about political values as much as housing policy, balancing the home ownership ideal against the desire to preserve social housing for future generations.

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set out the plans in the House of Commons Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to overhaul immigration rules.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Proposals for stricter requirements to qualify for permanent settlement in the UK were first outlined in detail in November 2025, when Mahmood was home secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: She has argued that settlement should be "earned", rather than being granted automatically, with those who contribute more to the country able to settle fastest.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Following a consultation , external , Mahmood has now announced her final decision on what changes should be taken forward.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Elements of her original proposals have been revised following a backlash from some Labour MPs, with plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for settlement scrapped.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) – also known as settlement – gives someone the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the current system, people with ILR can also apply for benefits if they are eligible.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: People who have lived in the UK for 12 months after being given ILR can apply for British citizenship, if they also meet other requirements , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the government's plans, the standard length of time migrants will have to live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement will double from five to 10 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under this 10-year pathway, applicants must have earned at least £12,571 for five of the seven years immediately before being granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Migrants who have claimed certain benefits or breached immigration rules will only be able to settle after at least 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Adults with a criminal record will be refused settlement, with discretion to refuse cases where the offence was committed when the applicant was under 18.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK through an official government scheme will qualify for settlement after five years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, other refugees will need to wait 10 years and either work or study.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Those who do not work or study will need to wait 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they don't.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The changes will apply to migrants who are already in the UK but not those who have already been granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: A partner who arrives with someone who then applies for ILR will be able to settle at the same time, as long as they meet the relevant requirements.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, a partner who joins later will need to complete the same qualifying residence period before they are eligible for settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Eligible couples will be able to combine their earnings to meet the minimum income  requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The household income threshold will be £25,142 – twice the individual minimum income requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Children under 18 will continue to be able to settle with their parents.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: They will be exempt from the income, government debt, English language and Life in the UK test requirements, but will remain subject to the relevant suitability and criminality requirements.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Young adults aged 18 to 24, who remain dependant on their family, will also continue to be able to settle alongside them.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: They will be expected to meet all the adult mandatory requirements but not the individual income requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Someone who is aged 25 or over when their family becomes eligible for settlement will be expected to qualify independently.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Eligible partners, parents and children of British citizens will continue to qualify for settlement after five years.

sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Morgan pointed out that cocaine death figures included not only those who snorted the drug but also users who injected it or smoke crack cocaine in combination with opioids or counterfeit pharmaceutical drugs.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "The small decline in deaths related to cocaine should not be over-interpreted.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Most important is that deaths relating to cocaine remain roughly quadruple what they were in 2015 and are now more frequent than deaths relating to heroin or morphine," he said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Meanwhile, ketamine was referenced in 115 deaths last year - almost double the year before and up from just seven fatalities 10 years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Morgan said this was down to lower prices and use of the drug becoming normalised.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: He said there were increasing reports of young people becoming dependent on ketamine and suffering acute health difficulties such as bladder damage.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Anthony Irvin (pictured with sister Nyk) died from drug poisoning in 2025 Mike Trace, CEO of the addiction charity Forward Trust, said drug poisoning deaths remained high because of factors including the proliferation of very strong synthetic opioid drugs called nitazenes .
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "We know that increasingly potent drugs like nitazenes are making their way on to the market.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: We know that established drugs like cocaine are growing in purity which means they come with much higher risks to users," he said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Nitazenes can be many times more potent than heroin and have been linked to hundreds of UK deaths.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Tom Powell and Nyk Irvin's brother Anthony Irvin died from drug poisoning in Ramsgate in September 2025 at the age of 52.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: His siblings believe his death was caused by a supply of drugs being contaminated with synthetic opioids, but say delays in blood testing mean they will never know for sure.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Today's figures are shocking," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "We are fighting to wake people up to the scale of the problem."

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A positive result does not automatically mean there is cancer, and a negative result is not a guaranteed all-clear.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Health secretary Yvette Cooper said she hoped simple blood tests such as these would help identify patients needing urgent investigation much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Michelle Mitchell from Cancer Research UK said: "GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need." sentences.text: Two-year-old Finlay Roberts died after spending hours in a crowded hospital corridor.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner raised concerns about a lack of basic observations done by busy staff.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A new early warning system is being introduced in hospital emergency departments in England to help busy NHS staff identify sick children who are dangerously deteriorating.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A high overall score means a child needs more urgent attention.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Concerns from staff, parents, carers or the child themselves will trigger an immediate escalation of care.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: It comes after Health Secretary Yvette Cooper promised to stop "corridor care"  for sick children because of long waits for hospital beds.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The new National Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS) asks staff to check, log and grade vital signs, such as blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The initiative is designed to save lives ahead of winter, when pressure on the NHS is at its highest.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: On the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper recently talked about the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts, who died in 2024 after spending hours in a hospital corridor before being discharged.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Cooper apologised to Finlay's parents on behalf of the NHS, saying: "No child should be treated in a corridor.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner raised concerns about a lack of basic observations done by busy staff , external .
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Martha Mills died aged 13 at King's College Hospital in London in 2021 A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Duncan Burton, chief nursing officer for England, said the new early warning system for children in emergency departments was an "important next step in improving care for children and young people across England for this winter - and beyond".
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: He added: "In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child's condition is deteriorating.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: "This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters." The early warning system for children, PEWS, is a collaboration between NHS England and the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health and the Royal College of Nursing.

sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves contain toxic compounds, while tough stalks and seeds may not be suitable for young children.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She says that would "catch" more people with low vitamin D and give a more accurate picture of how widespread the issue is.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday warns of "a lifelong deficit" in women - in adolescence, then pregnancy, and then the newborn is affected.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: He tells me that despite being 100 years on from the discovery of vitamin D "rickets hasn't gone away".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If we have rickets in the community, there are going to be many more people who are vitamin D deficient." He says the government should look into wider fortification of food in which vitamins are added to foods during production.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Countries like Canada and Sweden have mandatory policies.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, some foods such as breakfast cereals and spreads are already fortified with vitamin D, but it is voluntary.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: During the winter months, people start to lose their vitamin D levels.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "We might have to accept that for certain groups vitamin D supplementation is a matter of course," says Hewison.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia is now taking vitamin D supplements regularly - and is back in goal.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: This video can not be played Min says people do not always understand her sacrifices and how valuable support is A young carer says she feels burnt out, and forgotten about by friends as she takes on extra tasks at home.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: Madeline, 16, from Bridgend, cares for her mum and granddad, a role she says she is happy to do.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: But she has said people do not always understand its mental impact, and believes both formal and informal support is "crucial" to young people.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: She is one of an estimated 170,000 young carers in the UK aged five to 17, but the Carers Trust calls that number the "tip of the iceberg" , external .
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: The Welsh government said its latest strategy, which is expected to be published this month, had a particular focus on young carers and recognises their contributions.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: Madeline, also known as Min, is one of 8,200 young carers in Wales.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: The 2021 census said there were about 120,000 young carers in England and 42,000 in Scotland.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: She is still at school and hopes to be a paediatric doctor one day.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "For me, being a young carer involves helping my mum get up in the mornings, making sure my mum and my granddad have had their medication," she said.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "It also involves cooking meals for my mum, my granddad or my siblings.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "There's also the cleaning which I'll do, any household job really no matter what it is." She said it can be difficult and often people do not understand what being a young carer entails.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "I find that my friends that aren't young carers don't tend to understand and that I can't always go out when they want or stay out to a certain time so I get kind of pushed aside and forgotten by my own friends," she added.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "Then there's the mental like side effects and stuff because obviously I'm caring about everyone else and I don't often tend to have time for myself." Min says friends struggle to understand the role of young carers Min said support, both formal and informal, "means the world" to young people like her.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: When she was eight, Min was referred to Bridgend Carers' Centre, which is partly funded by Children In Need , external , which gives her respite and a chance to socialise with other young carers.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: Without this, and support at school, Min said she "couldn't cope".
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: She said: "The young carers' group is so important to me because all my close friends that actually know what I go through, I get to see in these groups.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: She said: "It's shocking [to be] one of a handful of kids to be chosen, it's like, I'm one of the only people that are gonna be able to say I've sung with Children in Need and I'm so excited to be a part of it.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "It has opened her whole life up," she said.
sentences.article_title: I'm burnt out and feel forgotten as a young carer

sentences.text: "When I was told that I wasn't a 100% match, you're automatically thinking, 'God, what's going to happen next?' "But the fact that I could go into that sharing scheme – I had absolutely no issue with that.

sentences.text: "At the end of the day, if you actually think about it, two lives were saved in one day.

sentences.article_title: I saved a stranger's life and my husband's at the same time

sentences.article_title: I saved a stranger's life and my husband's at the same time

sentences.article_title: I saved a stranger's life and my husband's at the same time

sentences.text: Sean had lived "an amazing life" for 37 years before the kidney's function started to deteriorate.

sentences.text: Hannah Magowan said Belfast was described as the "capital" of kidney sharing Hannah Magowan, one of the specialist transplant surgeons at Belfast City Hospital, who performed Sean's transplant and helped with Una's surgery, said the sharing scheme had been operating in Northern Ireland since 2010.

sentences.article_title: I saved a stranger's life and my husband's at the same time

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Plans to sell land and farms in Devon had already caused upset among tenants on the Duchy estate Plans by the Prince of Wales to sell off up to 20% of the Duchy of Cornwall could see more tenant farmers across England asked to buy their farms or move out.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: Up to 40 farm holdings across Devon, Cornwall, Herefordshire and the Midlands could be affected by the sale, according to the Tenant Farmers Association (TFA).
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: Locals say talks over the future of nine farms on the Bradninch estate in Devon have already caused "distress" for some tenants who fear they cannot afford to buy.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: A spokeswoman said the Duchy could not confirm the total number of tenants affected by the ten-year sale plan , external but told the BBC the estate was "supporting them through the process with care and respect".
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: Former GP Mary Ryan, a local Lib Dem councillor who has lived near the Bradninch estate for around 35 years and is supporting the farmers, said some of those affected were "experiencing enormous mental and emotional distress" as a result of the planned sell-off.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: She added that while the Duchy had reportedly apologised to tenants last month, the handling of the process had been "pretty dire".
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: The sales programme has now been extended from Bradninch, near Cullompton, to the Duloe Estate in Cornwall and to individual holdings elsewhere in Cornwall, Herefordshire and the Midlands, according to the TFA.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: The Duchy's rural director, Matthew Morris, told the BBC he was listening to feedback over how the sales were being handled and offering support and mental health advice to tenants.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: Morris added that the Duchy was "still committed to agriculture" but that there "may well be other disposals in the future".
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: In terms of immediate evictions, he said, there were "no cliff edges here" and that the Duchy was working closely with every tenant to find a suitable outcome.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: "In the main, our mission is to sell to our farmers.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: We are keen that wherever possible we can achieve that continuity," Morris explained.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: "For many of our farmers, it's a generational aspiration to own their farm.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: A few people have said it to me: 'My grandfather wanted to buy his farm.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: My father wanted to buy the farm.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: And now I've got the opportunity and it's an amazing outcome'.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: "That's kind of what's driving me through what, at times, has been a little bit of turbulence." The Duchy - which was established in 1337 - currently has around 700 agricultural lettings, with around 300 whole farm holdings made up of a farmhouse, land and buildings.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: Farmers are on a mix of contracts ranging from time-limited to lifelong, with an option to pass the tenancy down through a family.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: George Dunn, TFA chief executive, said the organisation was in "deep discussions" with the Duchy and that poor communication had led to tenants "facing prolonged uncertainty over valuations, timing and the options available to them".
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: "Once a family is told that its long-term relationship with the Duchy may change permanently, that uncertainty lives with them 24/7," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: He added that while he welcomed the Duchy's assurance that "nobody will be made homeless" not every tenant "will be able or want to buy the farms that they operate and fair alternatives must be explored for those for whom ownership is unaffordable".
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: A spokeswoman for the Duchy said: "We are engaging with people directly and supporting them through the process with care and respect.
sentences.article_title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off

sentences.text: "We recognise that each of our tenant's circumstances are different, and we are taking a careful, case-by-case approach." Prince William selling 20% of duchy property for housing and nature projects Royal land set to be sold off in Devon
